problem_text:
A manufacturing network aims to devise a production quality enhancement strategy to lower total defect output from several assembly lines. Initially, no improvement techniques have been implemented.

The operational parameters for each assembly line are as follows:
* For Line A, defect rate per unit is 2.671, throughput is 160.117.
* For Line B, defect rate per unit is 1.727, throughput is 96.091.
* For Line C, defect rate per unit is 2.682, throughput is 62.844.
* For Line D, defect rate per unit is 1.935, throughput is 285.266.
* For Line E, defect rate per unit is 1.673, throughput is 169.432.

To reduce defects, several improvement protocols are available, each characterized by a specific defect reduction effectiveness:
* By deploying Protocol Alpha, defects will be decreased by 24%.
* By deploying Protocol Beta, defects will be decreased by 58%.
* By deploying Protocol Gamma, defects will be decreased by 84%.
* By deploying Protocol Delta, defects will be decreased by 40%.
* By deploying Protocol Epsilon, defects will be decreased by 86%.

Implementing a protocol on a line incurs an additional cost per unit of throughput. The cost matrix for all line–protocol combinations is provided below:

| Line \ Protocol | Protocol Alpha | Protocol Beta | Protocol Gamma | Protocol Delta | Protocol Epsilon |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Line A | 38.348 | 116.94 | 67.729 | 198.844 | 32.506 |
| Line B | 155.244 | 125.2 | 160.241 | 52.881 | 109.289 |
| Line C | 95.598 | 94.117 | 173.432 | 198.106 | 68.022 |
| Line D | 127.995 | 125.83 | 150.617 | 190.042 | 49.48 |
| Line E | 50.095 | 135.481 | 39.841 | 43.025 | 24.262 |

It is permissible to select multiple protocols for any given line, and a line may also operate with only partial improvements if required. The objective is to guarantee that the aggregate defect output is diminished by at least a fraction P = 0.201 of the initial defect level, while simultaneously minimizing the total incremental expenditure.
